text:
emma (platform): Proposal: new route matching DSL for gateway. Add capture vars, negation, and explicit priority numbers. Trying to avoid brittle implicit specificity rules. TL;DR: `match` blocks with `host`, `path`, `service`, `headers`; support `!` for negative patterns and `@` for captures. Example below — please skim and mention obvious pitfalls. :thinking:

raj: Nice. Can you paste a real example? also prefer explicit `priority` field so we can reason about overrides instead of magic ordering.

emma (platform): Sure — example:
```
match {
  host: "api.example.com"
  path: "/v1/users/@userId/*"
  headers: {
    "x-feature": "blue"
    "x-internal": "!true"  # negation: only when header not true
  }
  priority: 30
  backend: users-v2
}

# negative-only rule to exempt admin area from wildcard rule
match {
  path: "!/admin/*"   # `!` prefix to exclude
  priority: 50
}
```

lina: A couple concerns: 1) Negative path patterns can be surprising when combined with host globs (order matters). 2) We need well-defined conflict resolution when two matches both capture same var (e.g., `@userId`). What happens to capture precedence?

kai: For cost: avoid general regex as default. We should support 3 pattern flavors: `glob` (default), `prefix`, and `regex` (explicit opt-in). Regex routes should be traceable and rate-limited to avoid perf blowups.

morgan: UX note — Console should surface `priority` with a small numeric badge and provide a simulation panel: paste a sample request and show which rule wins + captured vars. That helps product + SRE debug rollouts.

raj: Also: header-only routes (e.g., `x-experimental: true`) should be allowed to outrank path matches when `priority` indicates it. But we need a migration story: current implicit ordering -> explicit priority. How do we handle absent `priority`?

emma (platform): Default behavior: missing `priority` maps to computed specificity score (existing behavior) but we emit a deprecation warning and UI nudge. Encourage teams to set `priority` for critical overrides.

lina: Canary interaction — if a canary writes a negative rule to exclude traffic, it could accidentally block rollout. Maybe require `canary=true` flag and make negative rules non-destructive in canary mode (only simulated).

kai: Agree. Implementation notes: parser should canonicalize rules to a tuple (priority, explicitness, pattern-type, length) and we sort deterministically. Also store a stable UUID per rule to avoid subtle reorder-on-update effects.

morgan: For Console display, show `match_simulation` results per rule and diff view for rollouts (old vs new). Also expose an API endpoint for batch validation.

emma (platform): Devops-bot ran the parser on our staging policy set: it found 7 ambiguous rules and 2 negative overlaps. patch: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pulls/482. Please review.

devops-bot: parser v0.2 deployed to staging. Use `POST /internal/match/validate` with body `{ "rules": [...] }` — returns `warnings` + `resolved_order`. Note: regex rules are flagged with `perf_risk`.

raj: Quick question: how do captures surface to downstream backends? do we inject headers like `x-capture-userId`?

emma (platform): Plan: capture vars become request metadata and can be forwarded as headers optionally via `forward: { headers: ["@userId -> x-user-id"] }`. Default: not forwarded. Need security review for header injection.

lina: Also add tests for overlapping captures and ensure consistent behavior in both hosted and private deployments (VPC).

kai: I'd like a follow-up RFC for `pattern-type` semantics: exact rules for `glob`, `prefix`, `regex`, and how `**` vs `*` behave. I'll draft it.

morgan: Action items: 1) kai drafts RFC (this week) 2) emma wires up Console preview 3) raj + lina review PR 482 4) devops-bot add perf warnings to API.

emma (platform): Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll merge the parser fix to staging tomorrow and enable `priority` deprecation warnings in Console next week. :thumbsup:
